comparator.name: Law (Rechtsgeleerdheid)
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Year 1 contains ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses (60 ECTS), year 2 contains ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses (60 ECTS), and year 3 contains 42 ECTS of compulsory law, society, moot-court, comparative-law, labour-law, civil-procedure and thesis work plus an 18-ECTS minor or mobility window. Zero-credit Dutch-language testing, mentoring and the Tilburg Skills Lab are retained as programme features but excluded from the credit total. The page also lists a 30-ECTS exchange option without specifying which 12 compulsory ECTS it replaces; this decision therefore preserves the internally complete 42+18 standard minor structure and does not invent an exchange substitution.
components: Genuine 18-ECTS open minor or mobility space. Tilburg names Law in Practice and Law and a Sustainable Future among the substantive options; no single option is imposed on the comparator reconstruction.

alternatives.label: Law, society & legal institutions
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines all available UCR law courses with political, social, economic, historical, research and communication study, matching Tilburg’s defining emphasis on law in its broader social context.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Tilburg’s generalist Rechtsgeleerdheid degree: legal foundations and the available private, criminal, constitutional, European, international and human-rights law courses are integrated with politics, society, economics, history, research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Introductory politics, sociology, economics and ethics precede advanced EU politics, social theory, public economics, conflict study and research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Law and a Sustainable Future
alternatives.labelReason: Tilburg names Law and a Sustainable Future as a substantive minor and explicitly presents sustainable development as a programme interest; this route retains the UCR law core while concentrating its remaining study in climate, sustainability, environmental governance, communication, data and AI.
alternatives.concept: A distinct response to Tilburg’s Law and a Sustainable Future minor, combining the UCR law sequence with sustainability, environmental governance, climate communication, data literacy and AI-related study.
progression: GOSGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for GOSLAWJ211, GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ311 and GOSLAWJ312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. No other selected course carries a formal prerequisite. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Law, Society & Justice, Sustainability Essentials I, Climate Change, Dynamic Earth, Introduction to Data Science) are concentrated in semesters 1, 3 and 5, and level-3 advanced work (Principles of Private Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Governance of Sustainability, Research in a Sustainable Delta, Sustainable Farming & Innovation, European Union Politics) is concentrated in semesters 2-6, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied and governance-focused study where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: This route is grounded in Tilburg’s named 18-ECTS Law and a Sustainable Future minor and direct sustainability interest. Against the closest route it replaces twelve of twenty-four courses (90 ECTS) with sustainability, climate, environmental-governance, communication, data and AI study; against the practice route it likewise differs by twelve courses (90 ECTS).

alternatives.label: Law in Practice & Advocacy
alternatives.labelReason: Tilburg names Law in Practice as a substantive minor and foregrounds courtroom advocacy, legal decision-making and procedural skills. The UCR route combines its law core with transnational business law, negotiation, leadership and advanced persuasive communication.
alternatives.concept: A distinct response to Tilburg’s Law in Practice minor, retaining the broad UCR law sequence while emphasizing legal advocacy, negotiation, organisational practice, business law, applied communication and research.
progression: GOSGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for GOSLAWJ211, GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ311 and GOSLAWJ312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENBUSI311 (semester 4) and BENENTR312 (semester 5), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 3), BENBUSI311 and BENECON311 and BENLEAD312 (semester 4) and BENECON212 (semester 6), which formally require it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Sociology, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Economics, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy) are concentrated in semesters 1, 2 and 5, and level-3 advanced work (Principles of Private Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Transnational Business Law, Public Economics, International Business & Governance, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Persuasive Communication) is concentrated in semesters 3-5, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: This route is grounded in Tilburg’s named 18-ECTS Law in Practice minor and direct advocacy interest. It differs from the closest route by six courses each way (45 ECTS), replacing political and historical context with business, leadership, rhetoric and communication practice; it differs from the sustainability route by twelve courses each way (90 ECTS).

selection.assessment: The closest broad law-and-society route and Tilburg’s two named substantive minor directions are all evidence-backed, mechanically feasible and materially distinct. The closest match owns the eleven remaining generator-eligible programme interests; Law and a Sustainable Future owns rows 9502 and 9506; Law in Practice owns rows 9504 and 9507. The alternatives differ by at least six courses each way (45 ECTS), exceeding the pairwise floor, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Tilburg’s Rechtsgeleerdheid is a Dutch-law degree with a continuous doctrinal sequence, procedural-law practice, a zero-credit Skills Lab, an integrated moot court and an 8-ECTS legal thesis. UCR can assemble a substantial interdisciplinary law pathway across private, criminal, constitutional, EU, international and human-rights law, but it does not reproduce the full Dutch professional-law curriculum or its integrated practice sequence.

UCR has no dedicated equivalents for Tilburg’s Dutch administrative-law procedure, tax law, property and contract sequence, liability law, labour law, civil procedure, legal-history sequence or integrated Skills Lab and moot-court training. Adjacent politics, business, communication, sustainability and technology courses broaden the UCR alternatives without being treated as direct replacements for those specialist components.

The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught and includes a compulsory zero-credit Dutch-language test; UCR is English-taught. The comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language eligibility.
